x: Pat's 13:00 mins beat the relay record by 2 secs; but this was not enough to erase Bob Roath's new mark of 12:55 set on the first stage. To complete the records our agregate time was our fastest ever.

Chris ran a good leg, gaining another place but losing some ground on Walton, who had gone well ahead through a fast run by Bob Roath. Charlie Walker gained 10 secs. on the leaders and brought us to 4th place with a typically solid effort on the 4th stage.
This was to be the race where Gerry North would clinch the individual title, but Gerry was injured and unable to run so the award went to Walton's Bob Roath.
Although Gerry won three of the races, he did not qualify for the individual award as he did not compete in all 4 races - this went to Walton's Bob Roath for the 2nd successive year.
Bob Roath,Jim Derham,F.Maillardet and Ian Macintosh were together for the first sixteen miles and it was only in the last four miles that this quartet began to split,Bob Roath proving the strongest.

Those that showed surprise last year when Bob Roath chopped our course record down to 1:45:53 were simply astounded on July 16th this year when 21 years old Graham Taylor of Cambridge Harriers re-wrote the record book with a truly outstanding 1:39:47.
